questions.question: What is total internal reflection? State two conditions for it to occur.
questions.solution:
**Total internal reflection:** When light traveling from denser to rarer medium is reflected back into the denser medium at angles greater than critical angle.

**Conditions:**
1. Light must travel from denser to rarer medium (n₁ > n₂)
2. Angle of incidence > critical angle (i > i_c)
questions.knowledgeNote: Critical angle: sin(i_c) = n₂/n₁. For water-air: i_c = 48.6°. Fiber optics uses TIR.
questions.answer: **Total internal reflection:** when light travelling in the **denser** medium strikes the boundary with a rarer medium at an incidence angle **greater than the critical angle C**, it is completely reflected back into the denser medium — no refracted ray escapes, and the reflection obeys the ordinary laws of reflection. **Two conditions:** (1) the light must travel **from the optically denser medium toward the rarer** (e.g. glass → air, water → air); (2) the **angle of incidence must be greater than the critical angle** (sin C = 1/n for a medium-to-air boundary). **Deep point:** at exactly C the refracted ray grazes the surface; beyond C there is no real refracted direction, so all the energy turns back — the optical fibre's whole operating principle.
